name: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Development of heart failure in the last month of pregnancy or within 5 months postpartum
Absence of another identifiable cause of heart failure
Left ventricular systolic dysfunction with ejection fraction <45%, fractional shortening <30%, or end-diastolic dimension >2.7 cm/m²

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of preexisting heart disease is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: New onset systolic heart failure in peripartum period
Left ventricular dilatation with reduced ejection fraction

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal bloating due to hepatic congestion

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP
Elevated liver enzymes secondary to congestion
imaging: Echocardiogram showing left ventricular dilatation and reduced ejection fraction
Chest X-ray demonstrating cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion
Cardiac MRI may show myocardial edema or fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; some familial clustering reported
other: Electrocardiogram may show nonspecific ST-T changes or arrhythmias
Endomyocardial biopsy rarely performed, may show myocarditis or nonspecific changes

distinguishingFeatures: No temporal association with peripartum period
No new onset in peripartum period
Sudden onset dyspnea and chest pain

references: Demakis JG, Rahimtoola SH. Peripartum cardiomyopathy. Circulation. 1971;44(5):964-968.

Sliwa K, Hilfiker-Kleiner D, Petrie MC, et al. Current state of knowledge on aetiology, diagnosis, management, and therapy of peripartum cardiomyopathy: a position statement from the Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology Working Group on peripartum cardiomyopathy. Eur J Heart Fail. 2010;12(8):767-778.
Elkayam U. Clinical characteristics of peripartum cardiomyopathy in the United States: diagnosis, prognosis, and management. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2011;58(7):659-670.
